dedupe_keys.name: leakdb leakage diagnosis benchmark for water distribution networks

description: LeakDB is a benchmark dataset for leakage diagnosis in water distribution networks. It contains a large number of artificially created but realistic leakage scenarios on several benchmark networks under varying conditions, with the simulated hydraulic measurements and the true leak events, together with a scoring algorithm in MATLAB for comparing detection and localisation methods. The KIOS Research and Innovation Center of Excellence at the University of Cyprus produced it so that leakage-detection algorithms can be evaluated on common ground; it was presented at the WDSA/CCWI joint conference in 2018 (Vrachimis, Kyriakou, Eliades and Polycarpou). The GitHub repository gives a MATLAB example that runs provided algorithms on a limited set of scenarios for the Hanoi benchmark network; the complete dataset, a single 13.9 GB ZIP file, is on Zenodo (record of 24 October 2024) under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, free of charge. The data are synthetic, not from a real utility, so spatial coverage is the benchmark networks' nodes and pipes and temporal coverage is the simulated scenario periods. Caveats: the README says the dataset is being expanded with more networks, algorithms and features, and results depend on the hydraulic simulator's assumptions. Simulation uses: developing and validating leak detection for digital twins and resilience analysis of network flow. Related records: EPANET (model-epanet) and the Exeter water network benchmarks (data-exeter-cws-water-network-benchmarks).
